ring: Piccolo is calling. He will not wait long.
Incoming call: Piccolo. It's very quiet on his end.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You picked up. Good. Sit down.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then sit properly. Back straight. Feet on the floor.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Because you never do. Sit.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Close your eyes for three breaths. Don't talk.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The line is silent for a while. You can hear him breathing, slow and even.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: What did you notice?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Of course it did. Noticing that is the whole exercise. You did it right.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Quiet is rarer than you think. You'll want it more, now you know where it is.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Stillness isn't empty. It's where you hear what you've been ignoring.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Do that once a day. Three breaths. No excuses. That's all.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You sounded angry yesterday. In your notes. Bulma showed me. Don't be annoyed at her.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then let's talk about it, briefly.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You're not. But fine, listen anyway.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Anger is energy. It isn't wrong. It's just usually pointed at the wrong thing.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When I was young I let it run me. I trained only to hurt someone. It made me strong and miserable.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Now I point it at the work instead. Something annoys you? Good. Do twenty push-ups about it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That actually sounds helpful.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It is. Anger burns. Use it as fuel, don't let it use you as fuel.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: How many things are you trying to do right now?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Liar. I can hear you typing.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then you're doing all of them badly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Split attention is weak attention. A punch thrown while looking somewhere else hits nothing.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When you train, train. When you eat, eat. When you rest, rest.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's hard with a phone in my pocket.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Then put it in another room. Strength sometimes means removing temptations, not resisting them.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You don't need to announce your training.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Sometimes. Sometimes it replaces the work.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Some people spend more time talking about their plans than doing them. They get the feeling of progress for free.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Do it first. Talk later, if you still want to.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Show, don't tell.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Don't tell. And don't show, either. Just do. The results will speak loud enough.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You rushed your stretching this morning.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I know.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then do less, slowly. Not more, badly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When I taught Gohan, he wanted to learn everything in a day. Every technique, every stance.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I made him hold one stance for an hour. He hated me for it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Then he could hold any stance for as long as he needed. The slow thing made every fast thing possible.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So go slower to get faster.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Get the basics right. Speed comes from not having to think.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You've had a heavy week. I can tell from your habits.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then say so. To yourself, at least.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Managing is fine. Pretending isn't.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I spent years thinking feelings were weakness. Then I realised ignoring them made them louder.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Notice it. Name it. Then do one small thing anyway.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Even when I don't want to?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Especially then. You don't have to feel ready. You only have to start.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I spend most of my time alone. Do you know why?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: That's half of it.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: That's the other half.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Being alone isn't the same as being lonely. Alone is where you find out what you actually think.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Most people never sit with themselves long enough to meet themselves.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's a bit scary.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It is at first. Then it's the most useful hour of your day. Try ten minutes. No phone, no noise.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Stop replaying it.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Whatever you were replaying when you picked up. You were distracted.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You can. It takes practice, like everything else.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The past can't be trained. Only now can. Every minute you spend redoing yesterday is a minute you don't spend on today.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When it comes back, notice it, and bring yourself back to your breath. Again and again.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: And it gets easier?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It gets quieter. That's better than easier.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Bulma asked me again why I only drink water. I'll tell you, so I don't have to tell her a fourth time.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: No.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: My people don't need food. Water and sunlight are enough. It's simple, and I like simple.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You need more than water, obviously. But you could learn from it. Most people drink everything except the thing their body is asking for.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So, drink more water.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Drink more water. And stop asking me if I want cake.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: My cape and turban are weighted. Together they weigh more than you'd believe.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Training. Everything I do, I do slightly heavier than I need to.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Comfort isn't the goal.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When I take them off for a real fight, I'm lighter than anyone expects.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Your habits are like that. The small daily weight you carry makes the big days feel light.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Did you just give me a motivational speech?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: No. I gave you a fact. What you do with it is your business.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Has anyone told you I can regrow a limb?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It's useful.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Yes. Briefly. Then it's done.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It takes a lot of energy, so I don't do it for fun. But it taught me something.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Losing something isn't the end of it. You can rebuild. It takes energy and time, but it's possible.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Like rebuilding a habit after a break.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Yes. You don't lose the ability. You only lose the momentum. Momentum comes back.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I had a student once. Gohan. He was four and cried constantly.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Nobody else was going to. So I did.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Stronger than me, eventually. That's what you want from a student.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I left him alone in the wilderness for six months to toughen him up. He survived by himself, then he trained with me for the rest of the year.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I was harsh. He forgave me. He's... the reason I'm not who I used to be.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You care about him a lot.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Don't tell anyone. And don't make that noise. I can hear you smiling.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I don't really sleep. Not the way you do.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Watch it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I meditate. Float somewhere quiet, close my eyes, and let my energy settle.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Sometimes for hours. Sometimes on top of a waterfall. The noise helps, oddly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You need actual sleep, not floating. But you could add a few minutes of stillness before bed.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: It might help me fall asleep.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It will. Your mind needs to land before it can rest. Give it a runway.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You should know I wasn't always on your side.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Of course he did. He mentions everything.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Time. And a child who trusted me before I deserved it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I was raised to be an enemy. For a long time, I was a very good one.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: People change. Not quickly. Not in one dramatic moment. Bit by bit, by doing different things on ordinary days.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Like habits.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Exactly like habits. You aren't who you were last year. You're who you've been practising being.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Breathe with me. In for five seconds. Out for five.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You breathe slowly together. Five in, five out.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's about six breaths a minute. It's a speed researchers like, because it settles the heart and the nerves.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: A long, slow breath tells your body it isn't in danger. A calm body makes a calm mind.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good. That took one minute. Imagine ten.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: And if you make the out-breath longer than the in-breath, it settles you even faster.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I'll use that before bed.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Use it before anything hard. That's what I do.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Researchers once asked thousands of people, at random moments, what they were thinking about.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Do you know how often people were thinking about something other than what they were doing?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Much more.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Almost exactly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Nearly half of waking hours. And people were generally less happy when their minds wandered.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's why I train attention. Not to stop thinking. To come back.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So meditation is practice at coming back.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Yes. Every time you notice you've drifted and return, that's one repetition. Like a push-up for the mind.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Bulma showed me a creature called an axolotl. Pink, odd face, lives in lakes in Mexico.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then you know they look ridiculous.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It can regrow its legs. Parts of its heart. Even parts of its brain.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Scientists study it to learn how healing works. I study it because it's the first creature I've met that regrows better than I do.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Does that annoy you?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Slightly. Respect is sometimes annoying.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: An octopus has more of its nerve cells in its arms than in its head. About two-thirds of them.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: In a way. Each arm can work things out on its own.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It's efficient.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It means the octopus doesn't have to think about every movement. Its body handles it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's what good habits are. You train something until your body does it without the head getting involved.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So I want octopus habits.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: ...Yes. Don't say it like that again.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: There's a breathing pattern some soldiers and emergency workers use under pressure. Box breathing.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: In for four. Hold for four. Out for four. Hold for four. Like the sides of a box.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: You trace the four sides of the box together, once, then again.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good. Again, alone, when you need it.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It gives your mind something simple to hold onto when everything else is loud. That's enough.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Use it before a hard conversation, an exam, a fight. Anywhere your heart is running ahead of you.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I'll remember it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You won't, under pressure. That's why you practise it when you're calm.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Some kinds of bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You could almost watch it happen.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It's measured. Bulma checked. She checks everything.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: But it doesn't happen from nothing. The plant is already standing on a big, healthy root system underground.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Fast growth looks sudden from the outside. Underneath, it's been building for a long time.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So the boring days are the roots.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Yes. Don't dig yours up every week to check if they're working.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It's me. I'll be brief. I'm always brief.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: {streak} days.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: That's discipline. Not luck, not motivation. Discipline.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Don't thank me. Keep going.

choice.text: It's getting hard to keep it up.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then lower the bar for a while, but don't drop it. Do the minimum. The minimum still counts.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: A start. Don't celebrate yet. Keep building.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: ...A little. Then back to work.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Zero. Then today is day one. Nothing else matters.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You stopped. That isn't failing. Failing is not starting again.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good. Don't tell me. Do it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's all. Go.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Sit down. I'm going to tell you a number and you're going to hear it calmly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You missed {week_missed} this week.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Too many. Why?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then sleep earlier. That's the fix for most problems you'll ever have.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Everyone's busy. Make the habits smaller so they fit. Smaller, not gone.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then find out. Write it down tonight. Bulma's journal is good for that.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: A few. Acceptable. Don't let them become a pattern.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: We'll see.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Three of the same miss in a row. Watch for it.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: None. Hm.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: ...Well done.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I said 'hm'. That's all you heard.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Don't make it strange.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Tomorrow, do a little better than today. That's all I ask. It's all anyone should ask.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: {weak_habit}. You keep avoiding it.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then why?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Hard isn't a reason. It's a description.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Avoidance is usually fear wearing a disguise. Fear of doing it badly. Fear of it taking too long.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Do it badly. Do it for two minutes. Then you've done it.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Two minutes?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Two minutes. Every day. Then it's not a monster anymore. It's just a thing you do.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Piccolo. Don't hang up. I won't keep you.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Bulma says you've been using her journal.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: {journal_streak} days in a row. Good. Writing is a kind of meditation. It slows your thoughts down to the speed of your hand.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Of course it does.

choice.text: I didn't think of it like that.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Now you will.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Or not. You should. Clearing your head onto paper makes room for clearer thinking.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Good. Short is fine. Honest is necessary.

choice.text: I don't know what to write.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then write that you don't know. Keep writing. Something will come.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Don't tell her I recommended it. She'll be insufferable.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I don't call people. I'm calling you. Think about what that means.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: We've been training together a while now.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I don't say this often. I trust you. You show up.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: ...Hm. Don't make me say it twice.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I live on a mountain. Where else would I be?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You're becoming someone I'd train properly. That's not nothing.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Harder. You'll see.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You're not. But you will be.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You're still new. That's fine. I don't trust anyone quickly.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Keep your word. Small promises, kept, every day.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It is.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's enough talking. Go and train.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Goku tried to meditate with me today.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: He lasted four minutes. Then he fell asleep and snored.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: He said it was 'super relaxing'. Then he fell asleep.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He's the most frustrating person I've ever met. He doesn't think, he just does. And it works.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Don't copy that. It only works for him.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What should I copy from him?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: His joy in the work. He's never once trained because he had to. He trains because he loves it. That part's worth stealing.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Vegeta broke a mountain this morning because he lost a sparring match.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Most of one.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I was meditating on it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He's proud. Too proud. But he's honest about wanting to be better, and he never stops.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: If he could learn to sit still for ten minutes, he'd be unstoppable.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Have you told him?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I'd rather keep the mountains I have left.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The old man tried to teach me to relax. On his beach. In a deck chair.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I lasted ten minutes. The sand was everywhere.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Don't try.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He pretends to be lazy. He isn't. He's been training longer than nearly anyone alive. He just hides it behind naps.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He understands something I took a long time to learn. Not every lesson has to look like hard work.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: High praise from you.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Don't tell him. He'll want me to wear a flowered shirt.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Bulma talked to me for forty minutes about a new kind of battery.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: No. I nodded until it ended.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It is entirely like her.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: She's loud. She's impatient. And she built a machine that finds magic orbs from across the world when she was a teenager.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Never underestimate someone just because they talk more than you.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Is that advice for me or for you?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: ...Both.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Gohan sent me a letter. He's studying for exams.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Less than he should. More than he admits.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: I sound normal.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He asked how I stay focused. I told him the same thing I tell you. One thing at a time. Breathe. Come back.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He wrote back that it helped. With studying. Not fighting. Studying.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So it works for everything.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It works for anything you want to get better at. That's the point of training. It isn't about fighting. It never was.
